body:
Today's scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities across the Kalshi and Polymarket gold books — a genuinely quiet day rather than a gap in the data. Spot gold itself is trading in the $4,335–$4,360 range as of this week (gold is currently trading at 4335.730, down 1.88% since yesterday... an ounce of Gold costs $4335.73), and that level lines up sensibly with where the Kalshi settle above ladder for September 30 is priced: the $4,290.99 strike sits near a coin-flip (51¢ bid / 57¢ ask), which is what you'd expect for a threshold close to today's spot with three weeks left on the clock.

One thing worth flagging rather than treating as free money: the Kalshi $4,130.99 and $4,170.99 above strikes for September 30 are both quoted at an identical 68¢ bid / 69¢ ask, even though a higher strike should always be worth less than a lower one on the same underlying and expiry. That's not a real edge — it's a symptom of a thin, infrequently-updated order book (both contracts show modest 24-hour volume), and by the time you tried to trade the size needed to matter, one side would almost certainly move. It's a good illustration of why the scanner requires a live, fillable order book before calling something an opportunity, rather than just comparing quoted mid-prices.

The Polymarket contracts in today's data use a different resolution rule entirely — touch (did gold cross $4,200 at any point in the month) rather than Kalshi's settle (where is gold at the exact 5:00 PM snapshot). Prices on the two can look inconsistent side by side without any arbitrage existing, simply because they're paying out on different events. Beyond that, the broader backdrop is a market near multi-month highs on dollar softness and rate-cut expectations (gold (XAU/USD) is trading near $4,400–$4,414, up roughly 0.9% over 24 hours and holding firm after climbing more than 1% the prior session), but nothing in today's contract pricing looks dislocated from that.
headline: Gold prediction markets show no real arbitrage despite a stale-quote wrinkle on Kalshi
